dedupe_keys.name: fao food loss and waste database

description: The FAO Food Loss and Waste Database collects measurements of how much food is lost or wasted along supply chains, from farms through transport, storage, processing, wholesale and retail to households, with the reported causes. Each data point gives the commodity, country, year, value chain stage, loss percentage, measurement method and source. The producer is the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations, a custodian of Sustainable Development Goal target 12.3, compiling scientific journals, grey literature, national reports and FAOSTAT. Coverage, as of January 2026, is almost 40,000 data points from more than 700 publications on 296 commodities in 167 countries, growing by about 2,400 points in 2025. Licence (read on the provider page on 2026-09-28): FAO terms: statistical databases fall under the FAO Open Data Licensing Policy and Statistical Databases Terms of Use (licence of this database not named on the pages read). Access is free of charge. Caveats: the points come from heterogeneous studies with different definitions and methods, many are small case studies that are not nationally representative, and coverage by stage and region is uneven. Simulation uses: loss rates for storage, transport and cold chain stages in food supply network and flow models, and parameters for resilience studies of post-harvest infrastructure. Related records: FAOSTAT food balances (data-faostat) give national loss totals, and EDGAR-FOOD (data-edgar-food) gives end-of-life emissions.
